title: Unit economics: add query API endpoints (time series + breakdowns) with pagination, caching, and access checks
author: Felix Schneider
release_notes: Internal-only: adds backend endpoints powering the Unit Economics dashboard (timeseries + breakdown queries) with RBAC/feature-flag gating, cursor pagination, and response caching.
body: Summary: This PR adds the Console backend query endpoints needed for the internal Unit Economics dashboard v1. It exposes (1) a time series endpoint for blended $/1M output tokens and supporting signals and (2) a breakdown endpoint for top-N/group-by drilldowns across model/model_version/quantization_profile, region, and customer_tier. The endpoints include cursor-based pagination, cache + rate-limit protections, and internal-only access checks (feature flag + RBAC). Motivation: Product/Finance need a consistent, fast way to query the warehouse/materialized views produced by the hourly aggregation job without issuing ad-hoc SQL. Engineering needs stable query semantics (dimensions + cardinality constraints) and predictable backend load. This PR is scoped to internal use only and intentionally avoids any customer-identifiable drilldowns. Endpoints: 1) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/timeseries - Query params: start (ISO8601), end (ISO8601), granularity (hour|day), filters[model], filters[model_version], filters[quantization_profile], filters[region], filters[customer_tier], include_signals (true|false). - Response: points[] where each point has ts, blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd, output_tokens, total_cost_usd, cache_hit_rate, batching_efficiency, avg_output_tokens, streaming_share, p50_latency_ms (where available). - Notes: granularity=day uses warehouse daily view; hour uses hourly view. include_signals gates optional columns; if missing coverage, fields are null but the point still returns. 2) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/breakdown - Query params: start, end, group_by (model|model_version|quantization_profile|region|customer_tier), sort_by (blended_cost|output_tokens|total_cost), sort_dir (asc|desc), limit (default 25, max 200), cursor (opaque), plus same filters[] as above. - Response: rows[] each containing dimension_value plus blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd, output_tokens, total_cost_usd, and optional signals; includes next_cursor when more results exist. 3) GET /api/internal/unit-economics/metadata (small helper) - Returns allowed dimension values and display labels (e.g., canonical region list, tier list, quantization profile allowlist) for UI filter dropdowns; backed by the same mapping tables used in aggregation to prevent UI/backend drift. Access control: - Feature flag: internal_unit_economics_dashboard (default off). - RBAC: requires permission console.internal.unit_economics.read. - Additional guardrail: requests must originate from internal auth context (no API keys); we validate session principal type and explicitly reject customer principals. - Audit log: emits an audit event on each request with principal, endpoint, filter/group_by, and time range; does not log raw SQL. Caching + performance: - Adds a small query-cache wrapper keyed by (endpoint, normalized filters, time range bucket, group_by, cursor). - Default TTL: 120s for timeseries, 300s for breakdown (matching expected refresh behavior in the UI). - Hard cap on lookback window for granularity=hour (max 31 days) to avoid expensive scans; UI uses day granularity for longer ranges. - Uses parameterized queries against the materialized views introduced by the aggregation job; no dynamic SQL concatenation. Pagination: - Cursor-based pagination for breakdown uses (sort_value, dimension_value) as a stable seek key; cursor is base64-encoded JSON of those values plus request hash to prevent cross-query reuse. - Enforces deterministic ordering (sort field then dimension_value) to avoid duplicates/missing rows across pages. Data safety / privacy: - No customer_id group_by or filter; explicitly rejected if passed (400). - The metadata endpoint only exposes pre-approved dimension lists (canonical regions, tiers, quant profiles); model lists are limited to Redwood-verified catalog IDs (no arbitrary strings). Implementation notes: - New query layer: UnitEconQueryService with methods queryTimeSeries() and queryBreakdown() and a shared normalizeFilters() function to ensure cache keys are stable and safe. - Warehouse view bindings are in analytics/sql/unit_econ_views.ts; time series selects only required columns depending on include_signals to minimize bytes scanned. - Adds request validation using existing schema util; invalid dims/tier values return 400 with a UI-friendly message. Tests: - Unit tests for filter normalization, cursor encode/decode, ordering stability, and RBAC enforcement. - Integration tests using a seeded test warehouse schema verifying: (a) timeseries output shape, (b) breakdown pagination returns consistent results, (c) cache hits do not bypass access checks, (d) rejecting disallowed dimensions. - Added load-test-ish test to ensure typical Finance view (7d, group_by=model, limit=25) stays under budgeted query time (asserts planner uses materialized view, not raw table). Screens/Examples (for reviewers): Example timeseries request: /api/internal/unit-economics/timeseries?start=2025-02-01T00:00:00Z&end=2025-02-08T00:00:00Z&granularity=day&filters[customer_tier]=hosted&include_signals=true. Example breakdown request: /api/internal/unit-economics/breakdown?start=2025-02-01T00:00:00Z&end=2025-02-08T00:00:00Z&group_by=region&sort_by=blended_cost&sort_dir=desc&limit=25. Rollout plan: - Behind feature flag, allowlisted for Engineering + Finance during dogfood (initial allowlist managed in ENG-8434). - Once UI (PR 19378) lands, we’ll enable the flag for broader internal audiences. - Monitoring: emits per-endpoint latency and cache hit-rate metrics; SRE will hook alert thresholds in the pipeline SLO work. Follow-ups / out of scope: - Finance ‘stable view’ vs ‘live view’ caching policy (separate TTLs and potentially separate endpoints) is not fully implemented here; this PR keeps TTLs conservative and relies on aggregation job freshness. - Reconciliation report endpoints (vs billing totals) are tracked separately (ENG-8430 / PR 19390).
commits: console-backend: add UnitEconQueryService and request validation
analytics: add parameterized SQL bindings for unit econ materialized views
authz: gate endpoints with feature flag + RBAC permission
api: implement timeseries endpoint + optional signals projection
api: implement breakdown endpoint with cursor pagination + deterministic ordering
cache: add query cache wrapper and per-endpoint TTL defaults
audit: emit internal audit events for unit econ reads
tests: add unit + integration tests for pagination, caching, and access checks
review_conversation: Chloe Martin (review): The endpoint shapes look good. Two nits: (1) ensure cache key normalization sorts multi-value filters so order doesn’t create cache misses; (2) we need a hard rejection if principal is customer-scoped. Please add tests.

Felix Schneider (author): Good call on filter ordering; added normalizeFilters() to sort arrays + canonicalize empty vs null. Also added principal-type assertion and a test that API keys are rejected.
Mei Lin (review): Can we guarantee the queries only hit materialized views? I’m worried about accidental fallback to raw hourly fact tables during refactors.

Felix Schneider (author): Added a guard in analytics/sql/unit_econ_views.ts to only reference mv_unit_econ_* objects. Integration test asserts the SQL contains mv_unit_econ_ prefix and the query planner uses the view in the test warehouse.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): RBAC permission name should match the bundle conventions (console.internal.*). Also audit logging should avoid logging full filter values (model names are OK; time ranges OK; but keep it minimal).
Felix Schneider (author): Updated permission to console.internal.unit_economics.read and trimmed audit payload to endpoint + group_by + time range + presence of filters (not the full list).
Allison Grant (review): Please add metrics for cache hit ratio and distinguish warehouse latency vs total handler latency. That will help SRE tune TTL later.
Felix Schneider (author): Added unit_econ_api.cache.hit, unit_econ_api.cache.miss, unit_econ_api.handler_latency_ms, and unit_econ_api.warehouse_latency_ms.
Jada Williams (review): Cursor should be tied to request parameters to prevent misuse across different filters/sorts. Also ensure stable tie-breaker ordering.
Felix Schneider (author): Cursor now includes request_hash; we validate it on decode. Ordering uses sort_value then dimension_value. Added tests for cross-query cursor reuse (400).
Chloe Martin (approval): Looks ready. Thanks for tightening access + tests.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main (commit message: "Unit economics: query API endpoints for internal dashboard").
